claims.text: The proposed method targets multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states at or near their melting temperatures.
A machine-learning approach can be used to generate EAM reference potentials for these alloys.
The generated EAM references can incorporate longitudinal spin fluctuations.
The generated EAM references can incorporate local lattice distortions.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations are relevant to finite-temperature behavior in high-entropy alloys.
Local lattice distortions mediate the representation of liquid atomic configurations.
Incorporating longitudinal spin fluctuations and local lattice distortions will improve representation of the many atomic configurations sampled by the ab initio liquid.
The machine-learning EAM references will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The machine-learning EAM references will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
TOR-TILD's EAM references constitute the baseline method.
The proposed method is applicable to equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method is applicable to non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method is applicable at temperatures up to 2000 K.
Experimental data for single-phase high-entropy alloys are limited.
The reliability of the proposed intervention is limited by the accuracy of the machine-learning model.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing machine-learning-based EAM references with traditional EAM references in molecular-dynamics simulations.
Failure to improve phase-space overlap and reduce path mismatch relative to traditional EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
